summary: Constructs finite positive moment measures for real C and actual bounded D inputs, with representation independence and weak descending-net continuity. They are not yet claimed to be geometric products.
detailedSummary: Proves mass and negative-shift error bounds, uniform extension, actual decreasing-representation independence, bounded-domain additivity, and a majorant formula. The descending-net theorem requires a common finite bound and a specified limit belonging to bounded D. No increasing closure, arbitrary infimum closure, flattening, measure-order monotonicity, total-variation convergence, Cartier comparison or locality is asserted.
text:
Use n1–n2. The positive rational test functional has mass B_u(1)=B_u(v(a)). For rational q>||f||_infinity, positivity of q±f gives |B_u(f)|≤q B_u(1), hence |B_u(f)|≤||f||_infinity B_u(1). Density from n1 extends it uniquely to a bounded real-linear functional on all continuous tests. Real linearity follows by rational scalar approximation. Positivity persists by approximating a nonnegative continuous function and adding a vanishing positive rational constant. The compact-Hausdorff Riesz correspondence identifies this functional with a finite positive Radon measure. This is ordinary functional background at its exact hypotheses; it supplies no geometric intersection theorem.

For rational tuples in [−M,0], input order against the constant −M gives
0≤B_u(v(J))≤M^p e_R(a repeated p times,J),
and mass≤M^p e_R(a).
For p=0 the factor is one. This is order of ideal-gauge moments, not order of measures.

If two rational tuples u,w in [−M,0] differ coordinatewise by at most epsilon, compare u_i−epsilon≤w_i and the reverse inequalities. Addition of the legitimate negative constant −epsilon=−epsilon v(a) and multilinear expansion give
|B_u(v(J))−B_w(v(J))|≤[(M+epsilon)^p−M^p] e_R(a repeated p times,J). (1)
Each nonempty subset S of shifted slots contributes at most epsilon^|S| M^(p−|S|) times that reference mixed multiplicity. Summing gives the displayed binomial expression. Use rational errors slightly larger than the actual error when necessary.

For arbitrary REAL C inputs, approximate uniformly by rational profiles. The approximants have a common bound [−M−1,0]. Estimate (1) makes every gauge moment Cauchy and independent of approximation. Difference-test values converge, positivity and the mass bound persist, and the resulting functional extends to a measure. Density and bounded masses give weak convergence on every continuous test. Passing to the limit with slightly enlarged bounds yields (1) for real C tuples. Symmetry, nonnegative real homogeneity, addition within the negative cone, and order on ideal moments pass to the limit. For addition approximate both summands and their sum; for real homogeneity approximate the scalar rationally. No singular transfer of BFJ multiplier approximation is used.

Now choose ACTUAL decreasing C-nets g_(i,alpha_i)→u_i for bounded u_i in D. Every representing term lies in [−M,0]. Use the finite product of their directed sets. For each ideal test v(J), its moments increase under refinement and are bounded by the preceding mass/moment estimate. Define B_u(v(J)) as their finite supremum. This is an increasing limit of bounded SCALARS, not an increasing function-class limit. Difference-test values converge by subtraction. Positivity and a common mass bound again give a finite positive measure, denoted nu_a(u_1,...,u_p).

Representation independence has an explicit compactness proof. Let g and f be two actual representations of the same bounded tuple. Fix indices beta_i and epsilon>0. The directed open sets {g_(i,alpha)<f_(i,beta_i)+epsilon} cover X_a because their limits satisfy u_i≤f_(i,beta_i). A finite subcover and directedness select one alpha_i for which the inequality holds everywhere. Thus g_(i,alpha_i)−epsilon≤f_(i,beta_i). Input order and the C shift expansion give
B_f_beta(v(J))≤sup_alpha B_g_alpha(v(J))+[(M+epsilon)^p−M^p] e_R(a repeated p times,J).
Take the supremum over beta, send epsilon to zero, and reverse the roles. All gauge moments agree, and density identifies the measures. The same proof with limits u_i≤w_i proves order on ideal-gauge moments throughout bounded D.

Addition of two actual decreasing C-nets, indexed by their finite product, is an actual decreasing C-net to their bounded sum. Hence that sum belongs to D by definition. Passing to scalar limits in C additivity proves bounded-D additivity. Scaling is handled similarly; scalar zero produces zero. Symmetry is immediate. The negative-constant expansion and (1) therefore remain valid on bounded D. No arbitrary nested-net flattening or infimum closure is used.

For each primary ideal J there is the exact formula
B_u(v(J))=sup{B_g(v(J)):g_i in C and g_i≥u_i for every i}. (2)
Every such majorant lies in [−M,0]. Order gives one inequality, while terms of a representing net give the other. This is a scalar formula and does not redefine D by all majorants.

The precise descending-net theorem is as follows. Suppose u_(i,lambda) in bounded D decreases pointwise to a SPECIFIED u_i in bounded D, and every term and limit has a common finite bound [−M,0]. Then nu_a(u_(1,lambda),...,u_(p,lambda)) converges weakly to nu_a(u_1,...,u_p). Membership of the limit is a hypothesis, not an inferred closure theorem.

To prove it, order bounds every gauge moment above by the target moment. Fix continuous C-majorants g_i≥u_i and epsilon>0. D functions are upper semicontinuous, so {u_(i,lambda)<g_i+epsilon} is open. These sets give directed covers. Compactness and the finite number of slots select one common lambda with u_(i,lambda)−epsilon≤g_i everywhere. Order and the bounded-D shift expansion imply
B_u_lambda(v(J))≥B_g(v(J))−[(M+epsilon)^p−M^p] e_R(a repeated p times,J).
Send epsilon to zero and take the supremum in (2). Gauge moments converge; density of their difference lattice and uniformly bounded masses give convergence on every continuous test. This is weak net convergence, not total-variation convergence.

Any globally zero entry annihilates the mixed measure for p≥1. Mixed-zero branch patterns belonging to G331's actual class are admitted. No unbounded or bottom input is added.

The conclusion is a bounded MOMENT-measure construction with proved continuity and algebraic presentation independence. Independent Cartier intersection comparison and actual open-set locality remain unproved. Artifacts: n3.md, argument.md, P12.4-paper.tex and native-notes.json. Rerun: python build_delivery.py.
